div.head: II Cn 35
div.ab: And freondleas man oððe feorran cuman swa geswenced weorðe þurh freondleaste, þæt he borh næbbe, æt frymtyhtlan, þone gebuge he hengenne ⁊ þær gebide, oð ðæt he gá to Godes ordale ⁊ gefare ðær þæt he mæge.

Be freondleasan. Gyf freondleas man oððe feorran cuman swa geswencad wurðe ðurh freondlæste, þæt he borh næbbe, æt frumtyhtlan, ðonne gebuge hé hengene ⁊ ðær gebide, oð þæt he gá to Godes ordale ⁊ gefáre ðær þæt he mæge.

And gif freondleas man oððe feorran cuman swa geswenced weorðe þurh freondleaste, þæt he borh næbbe, æt frumtihlan, þonne gebuga he hengcen ⁊ þær gebide, oð þæt he ga to Godas ordale ⁊ gefare þær þæt he mage.
Si quis amicis destitutus uel alienigena ad tantum laborem uenerit, ut plegium non habeat, in prima tíhla (id est accusatione) ponatur in carcanno et ibi sustineat, usque (donec) ad Dei iudicium eat.

Si aduena aut peregrinus, qui de longinquo uenit, sit tribulatus pro penuria amicorum, ut non possit habere plegios, ad primam calumniam, tunc subeat captionem regis et ibi expectet, quoad usque uadat ad iudicium ferri aut aquę illicque inueniat quod potest.

Et si quis alienigena uel suffragio amicorum destitutus adeo anxiatus sit amicorum penuria, quod fideiussorem habere nequeat, in prima accusacione, subeat suspendium et ibi prestoletur, donec adeat Dei iudicium et ibi proficiat quod poterit.

Be freondleasan. Gyf freondleas man oððe feorran cuman swa geswencad wurðe ðurh freondlæste þæt he borh næbbe, æt frumtyhtlan ðonne gebugé he hengene ⁊ ðær gebide, oð þæt he ga to Godes ordale ⁊ gefáre ðær þæt he mæge.

And gyf freondleas man oððe feorrancuman swa geswenced weorðe þurh freondleaste, þæt he borh næbbe, æt frymtyhtlan þonne gebuge he hengenne and þær gebide oð ðæt he ga to Godes ordale, and gefare ðær þæt he mæge.

(Von Sippelosen. B) Und wenn ein sippenloser oder fernher gekommener Mann durch Sippenlosigkeit so bedrückt wird, dass er keine Bürgschaft [für sich] erhält, dann, im Falle erstmaliger Beschuldigung, unterziehe er sich der Kerkerhaft und harre dort, bis dass er zum Gottesurtheile schreite, und erfahre [erlebe] hier, was er kann.

(Of men without kin. B) And if a man without kin or one come from afar is so hard pressed through lack of kin that he has no surety, then, at the first accusation, let him submit to imprisonment and wait there until he goes to God's ordeal, and fare there as he may.

Concerning the friendless. If a friendless man or one come from afar is so utterly destitute of friends as not to be able to produce a surety, on the first occasion that he is accused he shall go to prison, and wait there until he goes to God's ordeal where he shall experience whatever he can.

And if a friendless man, or a stranger from a distance, becomes so afflicted by his friendless state that he has no surety, he is then, at a first charge, to go to prison and stay there until he goes to God’s ordeal, and experience there what he may.

If a person who is friendless or come from afar is so bereft of friends as to lack a surety, on the first accusation he is to be suspended in chains and there abide until he undergoes God’s ordeal, and there suffer what he may.

Vom Klerus ohne Sippe (s. d. Gl 9. 29d) handelte I 5, 2c; über ‘freundlos’ s. VIII Atr 22¹. Phillpotts (Kindred 222) findet meine Übs. ‘sippenlos’ rash, wohl ‘zu eng’ meinend. Neben der Sippe ist höchstens noch eine rechtlich bestimmte Genossenschaft gemeint, sicher nicht das modern unbegrenzte, lediglich auf persönlichem Gefühl oder Handeln begründete Freundschaftsverhältnis

Clergy without kindred (see that word in Gl 9. 29d) were dealt with in I 5, 2c; on ‘friendless’ see VIII Atr 22¹. Phillpotts (Kindred 222) finds my translation ‘sippenlos’ rash, probably meaning ‘too narrow’. Besides the kindred, what is meant is at most a legally defined association, certainly not the modern, unlimited relationship of friendship founded merely on personal feeling or conduct

Untersuchungshaft im Gefängnis s. d. Gl 7. Inst drückt aus, dass dies stets öffentlich war, was ein Zeugnis aber nur für Heinrichs I. Zeit darstellt.—Dass Q das Wort nicht sofort verstand, zeigt dessen unübersetzte Herübernahme in erster Rezension, die in Hn vorliegt. Q's carcannum ‘Halseisen’ kommt zwar Anglonormannisch, aber vielleicht nicht Angelsächsisch vor. C's suspendium wird dafür anderwärts von Q gebraucht. Ein Abschreiber, der ‘Galgen’ missverstand, setzt deshalb eine Negation davor, da ja der Verdächtige im Texte weiter lebt

On detention in prison pending trial see that word in Gl 7. Inst states that this was always public, which, however, is evidence only for the time of Henry I. — That Q did not understand the word at once is shown by its being taken over untranslated in the first recension, which is found in Hn. Q’s carcannum ‘iron collar’ does occur in Anglo-Norman, but perhaps not in Anglo-Saxon. C’s suspendium is used by Q for it elsewhere. A copyist who misunderstood it as ‘gallows’ therefore puts a negative before it, since the suspect does, after all, go on living in the text
Ordal (s. d. Gl 22. 1d) ersetzt mangelnde Eideshilfe und besteht nur in Feuer und Wasser, wie hier Inst sagt, auch nach anderen Erklärern.—Letzte Zeile ebenso o. I 5, 2a. c

Ordeal (see that word in Gl 22. 1d) takes the place of lacking oath-help and consists only of fire and water, as Inst says here, and as other commentators also hold. — Last line likewise above I 5, 2a. c
